title: Octopus Social Tolerance Experiment
author: Eric Edsinger
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.w9nfh5e
materials: Monitor water conditions per instructions above daily.

steps.title: Maintain Octopus Housing and Water Quality
steps.instruction: House Octopus laqueus juveniles and adults in stable recirculating or flow-through seawater aquariums at densities up to 1 animal per 15 liters. Provide at least one medium or large clay pot per animal as a den. Match light cycles to local collection conditions.

substeps.instruction: Monitor pH, nitrates, and nitrites using a commercial kit.
Add PRIME per kit instructions if water quality declines rapidly.
Perform half-volume water changes daily to weekly based on water quality.

steps.title: Feed Animals
steps.instruction: Feed animals daily with live or frozen shrimp or crabs (live crabs preferred).

substeps.instruction: For short-term culturing: Transfer animals to individual Critter Keepers with a small clay pot, feed them outside the aquarium to minimize contamination, and transfer back.
For long-term culturing: Feed in stable tanks and remove carcasses 1-2 hours later.

steps.title: Prepare Elastomer Mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the elastomer injection mixture using a mixing container and popsicle stick.

substeps.instruction: Eject at least 1 mL of color component into the mixing container, measuring via syringe marks and recapping tightly.
Eject 1/10 of the color component volume of curing agent into the mixing container and recap tightly.
Mix thoroughly for one full minute with a popsicle stick.
Note: The mixture is usable for approximately 1 hour (depending on temperature/conditions) or can be kept on ice.

steps.title: Perform Elastomer Tagging
steps.instruction: Tag octopuses at least 24 hours prior to the social tolerance experiment.

substeps.instruction: Fill an autoclave pan or low-sided container with artificial seawater to a minimum depth of 5 cm to serve as an injection tank.
Place the octopus in a mesh bag and transfer the bag and container with seawater to a scale to tare it.
Record the weight and sex of the octopus (identify males by exceptionally large suckers on arms L2 and R2 and curling of the heterocautalus when walking).
Transfer the octopus in the mesh bag to the injection tank.
Gently collapse the mesh bag to position the octopus in a bottom corner and wedge it against the corner or wall of the tank.
Inject a small amount of elastomer into the dorsal mantle skin through the mesh bag, holding the syringe at a near-horizontal angle.
Verify the elastomer is secure in the skin.
Transfer the octopus in the mesh bag back to its tank and release it.
Check the octopus later that day or the following day to ensure full recovery and typical behavior.

steps.title: Set Up Social Tolerance Experiment
steps.instruction: Establish the experimental cohort and environment.

substeps.instruction: Select an appropriate number of octopuses of different sizes and sexes for the cohort based on tank size and specifics.
Place an appropriate number of clay pots in the experimental tank.
Transfer animals to the tank; Time 0 begins once all tanks and animals are set up.
Weigh animals at the start of the experiment.

steps.title: Conduct Experimental Maintenance and Monitoring
steps.instruction: Maintain the animals and record data throughout the experimental period.

substeps.instruction: Feed octopuses daily at a set time during or around the dark light cycle (when O. laqueus is most active), matching previous culturing times. Minimize light exposure during transfers (total of a few minutes).
Every 24 hours, a few hours after 'sunrise', score each tank and pot for octopuses, identifying individuals by elastomer markings. Repeat for several days or weeks per design.
Assess animals once to several times per day for stress or aggression (e.g., skin lesions or missing arm tips during feeding).
Log all observations per identified animal. If stress or aggression occurs, terminate the experiment per institute animal care guidelines.
Weigh the animals at the end of the experiment.
